prompt.context_jp: 富士山を背にした山梨県富士浅田市に、また新しい一日___始まる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 富士山を背にした山梨県富士浅田市に、また新しい一日___始まる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the opening narration.

feedback.correct_en: This is the chapter's opening line introducing a brand-new day as fresh information to the reader. が marks that newly introduced event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame 'a new day' as an already-established topic, which doesn't fit a scene-setting opener.

contrast_examples.en: A new day begins. (presenting fresh event)
The new day (as topic) is long.

prompt.context_jp: この町に暮らす遠藤清美と幼なじみたちの朝___、いつもと変わらぬような静けさに包まれていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: この町に暮らす遠藤清美と幼なじみたちの朝___、いつもと変わらぬような静けさに包まれていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the right particle after '朝' here.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence sets 'their mornings' up as the overall topic being described. は signals this topic frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the morning as new information, but here we are explaining what their mornings are like.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女たちの朝は静かだ。

prompt.context_jp: 休み時間の終わりを告げるチャイム___鳴っても、外で遊ぶ子供たちは なかなか教室に戻ろうとしない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 休み時間の終わりを告げるチャイム___鳴っても…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits before 鳴っても?

feedback.correct_en: The chime ringing is a new event being described in a subordinate clause. が marks this neutral-description subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'the chime' the topic, oddly singling it out when the main point is about the children not returning.

contrast_examples.jp: チャイムは学校の象徴だ。
contrast_examples.en: The bell is a symbol of schools. (topic)

prompt.context_jp: 店に着くと、みなぷーと はっち___すでに席についていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 店に着くと、みなぷーと はっち___すでに席についていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Kiyomi arrives at the restaurant. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Kiyomi walks in and discovers them already there — their presence is newly observed information. が fits this 'discovery' context.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat Minapu and Hacchi as the established topic, but we are presenting what Kiyomi sees upon arrival.

contrast_examples.jp: 行くと友達が待っていた。
contrast_examples.en: When I went, my friends were waiting. (discovery)

prompt.context_jp: 準備運動のために子供たちを整列させようとしていたとき、一人の児童___天井を指差した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一人の児童___天井を指差した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces 一人の児童?

feedback.correct_en: '一人の児童' (one of the pupils) is newly introduced into the scene. Indefinite one-time referents like this take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would require an already-known topic, but this child is being brought into the story for the first time.

contrast_examples.jp: 一人の男が入ってきた。

prompt.context_jp: 当時 まだ一年生だった はっち___、遠慮がちに 一歩前へ進み出た。
prompt.prompt_jp: 当時 まだ一年生だった はっち___、遠慮がちに 一歩前へ進み出た。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this flashback?

feedback.correct_en: Hacchi is being brought onto the flashback 'stage' as a new participant with a descriptive clause attached. が fits this scene-introducing use.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark her as the pre-established topic, but the narrative is spotlighting her stepping forward as a fresh action.

contrast_examples.jp: 背の高い男がやってきた。

prompt.context_jp: 中学の頃ほどの跳躍力___、もう腕にも脚にも残っていなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 中学の頃ほどの跳躍力___、もう腕にも脚にも残っていなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best fits here?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence sets up 'her middle-school jumping ability' as a topic and then contrasts it against the present ('no longer'). は carries that contrastive-topic feel.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would describe its absence as a neutral event, losing the implied contrast with her younger self.

contrast_examples.en: Her old strength is gone. (contrast with now)

prompt.context_jp: いつの間にか、天井には 三つのバレーボール___きれいに並んでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 天井には 三つのバレーボール___きれいに並んでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits before 並んでいた?

feedback.correct_en: This is a visual-discovery sentence: the three balls are observed, as a new situation. が marks the subject of this descriptive observation.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would awkwardly topicalize 'three balls' when the sentence is painting a scene that includes them for the first time.

contrast_examples.en: Flowers are blooming in the garden. (scene)

prompt.context_jp: 話___ 職員室じゅうを 早くも駆け巡り、別の学年の教師までもが 声をかけてきた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 話___ 職員室じゅうを 早くも駆け巡り…
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for '話'.

feedback.correct_en: 'The story' is already the ongoing topic (the ball incident the reader knows). は tracks that continuing topic as the sentence tells what it did next.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present '話' as newly spotlighted information, but it has already been established in the preceding paragraphs.

contrast_examples.jp: その話は学校中に広まった。
contrast_examples.en: That story spread through the school. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 押し問答が続いているところへ、事務室から 奥田の声___飛んできた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 事務室から 奥田の声___飛んできた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits before 飛んできた?

feedback.correct_en: Okuda's voice suddenly intrudes as a new event in the ongoing scene. が signals this fresh, sudden occurrence.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly treat the voice as a pre-established topic rather than a surprising interruption.

contrast_examples.jp: どこかから声が聞こえた。

prompt.context_jp: 入れ替わりに フロントへ入ってきた由美___、ふと思い出したように 口を開く。
prompt.prompt_jp: 入れ替わりに フロントへ入ってきた由美___、ふと思い出したように 口を開く。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle after 由美.

feedback.correct_en: The modifier 'who came in to swap places' introduces Yumi as a newly-entering participant in the scene, so が is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame her as the established topic, but the sentence is bringing her onstage with a scene-setting relative clause.

contrast_examples.jp: 遅れて来た田中が謝った。
contrast_examples.en: Tanaka, who came late, apologized. (new entrance)

prompt.context_jp: そんな清美___ ある日 勤務先の同僚 高橋孝介に 命を救われる。
prompt.prompt_jp: そんな清美___ ある日 勤務先の同僚 高橋孝介に 命を救われる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits after 清美?

feedback.correct_en: Kiyomi has already been introduced as the main character; this sentence comments on what happens to her. は continues her topic status.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight Kiyomi as new info, but the narration is extending our ongoing story about her.

contrast_examples.jp: 清美はある日助けられる。

prompt.context_jp: みなぷー___ 記憶を辿るように、店の天井のあたりへ視線をさまよわせた。
prompt.prompt_jp: みなぷー___ 記憶を辿るように、店の天井のあたりへ視線をさまよわせた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits after みなぷー?

feedback.correct_en: Minapu is the ongoing topic of this lunch-table anecdote; the sentence tells us what she does. は continues the thread.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce her as fresh information, but her storytelling has been the focus for several lines already.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女は天井を見上げた。
contrast_examples.en: She looked up at the ceiling. (topic)

prompt.context_jp: はっち___ 思いつく限りのチャンネル番号を、律義に並べ始める。
prompt.prompt_jp: はっち___ 思いつく限りのチャンネル番号を、律義に並べ始める。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle after はっち.

feedback.correct_en: The ongoing topic is Minapu's story; here Hacchi suddenly takes an action in that scene, so が highlights her as the new actor stepping in.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would reset Hacchi as the main topic, but Minapu's anecdote is still the discourse frame.

contrast_examples.jp: そこで妹が口を挟んだ。
contrast_examples.en: At that point my sister cut in. (new actor)

prompt.context_jp: 三人の視線___、自然と はっちに集まった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 三人の視線___、自然と はっちに集まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits before 自然と?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence describes a new event unfolding in the scene — three gazes converging on Hacchi. が marks that neutral descriptive subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 'three gazes' into a topic for commentary, but the point is the sudden movement itself.

prompt.context_jp: 洗濯物と掃除機を抱え直しながら、清美は そろそろ二人と落ち合う時間___思い出した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 清美は そろそろ二人と落ち合う時間___思い出した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits before 思い出した?

feedback.correct_en: 思い出す takes a direct object — the thing one remembers — marked with を. '時間を思い出した' = 'remembered the time'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be used with 思い出せる (potential), not with the active verb 思い出す. に doesn't fit this transitive pattern.

prompt.context_jp: 翌日の勤務中、清美はカウンターの裏で、高橋___ はっちの一件を切り出した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 清美はカウンターの裏で、高橋___ はっちの一件を切り出した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks Takahashi here?

feedback.correct_en: 切り出す ('broach a topic') directs the utterance toward a recipient — marked by に. Kiyomi raised the matter *to* Takahashi.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would make Takahashi the object of 'broaching', which isn't the grammar; で marks location/means, not addressee.

prompt.context_jp: “でも 人口は静岡のほうが 多いですけど”とか ちょっと ___ くんの
prompt.prompt_jp: ちょっと ___ くんの
prompt.prompt_en: The interviewer tries to provoke her. Which verb fits?

feedback.correct_en: あおる means 'to goad / stir up' — exactly what Minapu accuses the interviewer of doing by baiting rivalry.
feedback.incorrect_en: なだめる (soothe) and ほめる (praise) are the opposite of provocation and wouldn't match her annoyed reaction (うざっ).

prompt.context_jp: 制作の意図を ___ んだ
prompt.prompt_jp: 制作の意図を ___ んだ
prompt.prompt_en: The friends tease Minapu for playing along with the show. Fill in the verb.

feedback.correct_en: 意図をくむ is the set phrase for 'reading/respecting someone's intent' — the running joke of the whole scene (くんだねえ, くむよ...).
feedback.incorrect_en: 読む isn't the collocation used here (though 空気を読む exists); 知る just means 'know' and loses the nuance of accommodating intent.

prompt.context_jp: 子供たちに あおられ 元バレー部の血が ___
prompt.prompt_jp: 元バレー部の血が ___
prompt.prompt_en: The children egg her on and her old athlete instincts flare up.

feedback.correct_en: 血が騒ぐ is a set idiom meaning one's blood 'gets stirred up' — the exact feeling of her athletic urges kicking in.
feedback.incorrect_en: 泣く and 眠る aren't idiomatic with 血 and don't convey the surge of competitive excitement.

prompt.context_jp: “今 思えば あれが きっかけだった”ってなったら もう 悔やんでも ___ じゃないですか
prompt.prompt_jp: 悔やんでも ___ じゃないですか
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the expression that completes '悔やんでも...'.

feedback.correct_en: 悔やんでも悔やみきれない is a fixed emphatic idiom: 'no amount of regret would be enough'. Kiyomi uses it to dramatize the hypothetical.
feedback.incorrect_en: 悔やめない (can't regret) and 悔やまない (don't regret) flip the meaning and break the Vても〜きれない pattern.

contrast_examples.jp: 悔やんでも悔やみきれない。
泣いても泣ききれない。

prompt.context_jp: 先生って 1回 ___ ちゃったら もう 言うこと聞いて もらえなくなったりしますから
prompt.prompt_jp: 先生って 1回 ___ ちゃったら
prompt.prompt_en: Kiyomi explains why losing authority once is bad.

feedback.correct_en: ナメられる ('to be looked down on / disrespected') is the slang verb for losing authority with students — Kiyomi's exact worry.
feedback.incorrect_en: ほめられる (praised) is the opposite; 叱られる (scolded) doesn't fit a teacher being disrespected by pupils.

prompt.context_jp: 誰にも ___ られない秘密を共有することが、そのまま日常のリズムを刻み直したかのようだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 誰にも ___ られない秘密
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb completes 'a secret that can't be told to anyone'?

feedback.correct_en: 打ち明ける means to confide/reveal a private matter — the exact nuance of a secret you can't share.
feedback.incorrect_en: 話し合う is 'discuss (together)', and 思い出す is 'recall' — neither captures 'confess a secret'.

prompt.context_jp: こうなると なかなか ___
prompt.prompt_jp: こうなると なかなか ___
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb that fits — 'once this happens, it won't settle down easily'.

feedback.correct_en: 収まる ('to subside / die down') is the standard verb for a commotion settling, which is the narrator's point about the excited kids.
feedback.incorrect_en: 終わる just means 'end' with no nuance of calming; 止まる means 'stop moving', which is less idiomatic for a fuss subsiding.

prompt.context_jp: 情報 ___ の早いねえ
prompt.prompt_jp: 情報 ___ の早いねえ
prompt.prompt_en: A colleague comments on how fast news travels.

feedback.correct_en: 情報が広まる (news spreads) is the natural intransitive collocation for rumors propagating on their own.
feedback.incorrect_en: 届ける and 伝える are transitive ('deliver', 'convey'), which would require someone actively doing it, not news spreading by itself.

prompt.context_jp: 若葉が家を出る時。
prompt.prompt_en: Wakaba is leaving the house. Which exchange sounds more natural for a casual mother–daughter goodbye?

choices.text: A: 「いってきま～す」/「いってらっしゃーい」
B: 「出発いたします」/「お気をつけてお帰りください」

feedback.correct_en: A is the stock casual household exchange — exactly what the chapter uses between mother and daughter.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is overly formal business/ceremonial language, which would sound comically stiff at a family breakfast.

prompt.context_jp: はっちが子供たちに言う場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Hacchi strikes a deal with the kids. Which line sounds more natural in context?

choices.text: A: 先生 あのボール取るから みんな ちゃんと準備運動やるよ
B: みんなが準備運動をするために 先生があのボールを取ります

feedback.correct_en: A is the natural teacher-to-kids spoken rhythm — short clauses, 〜から/〜よ, and casual command. It's what the story uses.
feedback.incorrect_en: B reads like a translated written explanation; the 〜ために framing and full-polite verbs feel bookish, not spoken to elementary students.

contrast_examples.jp: 片付けるから、座ってて。
contrast_examples.en: I'll clean up, so stay seated. (spoken)

contrast_examples.jp: 片付けるために、座っていてください。
contrast_examples.en: Please sit so that I may clean up. (stiff)

prompt.context_jp: 清美が同僚の高橋に 無理なお願いを持ちかける場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Kiyomi is asking a hesitant favor from her coworker. Which phrasing sounds more natural?

choices.text: A: 高橋さん なんとか お願いできませんか？
B: 高橋さん なんとか お願いしてよ

feedback.correct_en: A matches the chapter: polite negative question (〜できませんか) softens a difficult request between workplace colleagues.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses casual 〜してよ, which is too familiar/pushy for a coworker you're imposing on with a weird favor.

contrast_examples.jp: 少し手伝ってもらえませんか？
contrast_examples.en: Could I ask for a bit of help? (polite request)

prompt.context_jp: 清美が若葉に、休日の予定を軽く聞く場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Kiyomi asks her daughter about tonight. Which sounds more natural between mother and teenage daughter?

choices.text: B: 帰宅時刻は遅くなる予定でしょうか？

feedback.correct_en: A is the natural casual family question used in the story — short, no polite ending, just the key word 帰り.
feedback.incorrect_en: B sounds like a business email or official form; no parent would phrase a kitchen question this way.

contrast_examples.jp: 本日の夕食は必要でしょうか？

prompt.context_jp: 清美が高橋に 事情を説明する場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Kiyomi defends her friend's problem. Which phrasing sounds more natural?

choices.text: A: はたから見れば しょうもないことですけど 本人にとっては 意外と深刻なことみたいですよ
B: 外部から観察すれば くだらない事柄ですが 当事者には重大事項に該当するらしいです

feedback.correct_en: A uses natural conversational phrasing: はたから見れば, しょうもない, 〜みたい — all fitting Kiyomi's spoken register with a coworker.
feedback.incorrect_en: B stacks heavy Sino-Japanese nouns (外部, 事柄, 重大事項, 該当) that sound like a written report, not a hallway conversation.

contrast_examples.jp: 本人にとっては大事なんだよ。
contrast_examples.en: To the person involved, it matters. (spoken)

contrast_examples.jp: 当事者にとっては重大な案件である。
contrast_examples.en: For the party concerned, it is a serious matter. (written/formal)
